behavior.task: spawn[T](fn() -> T) runs on a shared pool of daemon threads; await() rethrows a failure inside the task as Error; await_or(fallback) never throws
behavior.pool: pool(threads) runs tasks in submission order on that many daemon threads; shutdown() lets running tasks finish; a shut-down pool rejects spawn_on with Error
behavior.ordering: await_all and parallel_map return results in item order whatever the threads do
behavior.channel: bounded; send blocks while full and fails on a closed channel at run time; receive blocks and returns null once closed and drained; values are never null
behavior.counter: AtomicLong semantics on Int: get, set, add, increment, decrement, compare_and_set
behavior.lock: reentrant mutual exclusion: run(fn() -> Unit) and locked[T](lock, fn() -> T)
behavior.latch: count_down lowers, await and await_within(millis) wait for zero
behavior.errors: task bodies have no throws clause; library functions a task body calls (send, receive, sleep, run, locked) have none either and report invalid arguments at run time
behavior.threads: all threads are daemon threads: an ending program does not wait for unfinished tasks
